From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 14:15:00 +0000
Subject: Scheduling technical deep dive (US / EU / APAC overlap)

Hi Anita —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The customers engineering team asked for a deeper technical session with our solutions engineers to walk through: model selection, deployment patterns (Dedicated vs Private), and inference cost/latency tradeoffs for your peak workloads.

We want to include Marissa (solutions engineer) and Dev (infrastructure lead) from our side — copying Marissa. To make this effective we need a ~90 minute slot where at least two of your architects can join (you mentioned folks in EU + APAC). I know timezone overlap is a pain — particularly right now with DST differences between US/EU and APAC.

Initial thought: propose 2 possible windows next week (please tell me which works best and who will join):
- Option A: 16:00–17:30 CEST (Central Europe) — corresponds to 07:00–08:30 PDT (US West) / 23:00–00:30 JST (Japan)
- Option B: 08:00–09:30 CEST — corresponds to 23:00–00:30 PDT (previous day) / 15:00–16:30 JST

We included one late-evening option so your APAC architect(s) can join, and one mid-day EU option that might be easier for EU/US overlap (US would be early morning). If neither works, please share preferred 2-hour blocks in local time and we'll map overlaps on our side.

Attached is a short agenda and a checklist of artifacts we'd like (sample traffic profile, preferred models, any compliance constraints).

Best,
Sean Gallagher\Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@acme-analytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lars Jensen <lars.jensen@danske.dk>, Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@zenit.co.jp>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Scheduling technical deep dive (US / EU / APAC overlap)

Hi Sean —

Thanks — this sounds great. Quick notes on attendee availability:
- Lars (PI lead) is in Copenhagen (CEST) and prefers afternoons (15:00–18:00 CEST).
- Kenji (APAC architect) is in Tokyo (JST) and is available after 16:00 JST but prefers not to run past 23:30 JST.
- I (Anita) can be flexible, US early mornings are ok.

Given those constraints, Option A (16:00–17:30 CEST) looks the most promising — it puts Lars at 16:00 CEST (good), Kenji at 23:00 JST (a bit late but within his window), and will be early for our US stakeholders.

One caveat: our internal security reviewer flagged that if the session includes details on our retention/compliance setup we might need the security lead to join — could be a short 15-min block near the end. I'll try to confirm.

Can you loop in your SE (for deep architecture questions)? Also, sounds like Daylight Saving shifts caused a couple of our previous attempts to land at the wrong UTC — thanks for listing explicit offsets.

Anita
Sr. Product Ops, Acme Analytics
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Thanks Anita — this is helpful. Looping in Marissa (SE) and Dev (infra lead) to confirm availability.

Marissa / Dev — Anita's team prefers Option A (16:00–17:30 CEST) which on 2026-07-02 maps to: 07:00–08:30 PDT / 16:00–17:30 CEST / 23:00–00:30 JST. Can you confirm whether a 90-minute slot starting at 07:00 PDT on Thursday 2 July works for you? Note the late JST end time. If that's too late for us, we can try the Option B-style overlap but it pushes Kenji into mid-afternoon JST (which may work).

Agenda (attached): 10m intros, 40m architecture deep dive (model variants, batching, KV caching), 25m deployment & cost discussion (dedicated vs private), 15m security/compliance Q&A. If Anita's security reviewer wants to join for the last 15, we can leave that slot open.

Attachments: acme-deep-dive-agenda.pdf

If everyone confirms, I'll send a calendar invite with a Google Meet link and include the Drive folder with pre-reads. Sean
